verdict.rationale: Render documents Blueprints, which let you "define, deploy, and version your entire architecture with a single YAML file" (render.yaml) for multi-service architectures. The CLI can validate these files, and a community user independently praises the docker-compose-like infrastructure-as-code they keep under version control. missing for 10: in-depth first-party documentation of the Blueprint schema and which resource types it covers, and evidence of how version history or rollback of the Blueprint itself works.

support.subject: As a devops-lead, I can define, deploy, and version my entire architecture with a single configuration file

citations.quote: Define, deploy, and version your entire architecture with a single YAML file.
Manage your multi-service architecture with a single YAML file.
One of the biggest appeals to me is their simplified, docker-compose like approach to infrastructure as code... I still like to have it as code under version control
